In light of the reproductive brook trout fishery near Hwy. [13, no borrow areas should be allowed above Hwy. 171. It is further requested that the FPC investigate and control the present practice of using loose fill to stabilize road fills on Hwy. 171 and 413. This recent highway maintenance has discharged many pards of fill into the Howard Creek and makes preconstruction habitat studies invalid because of sedimentation impacts.
It is further requested that the proposed transmission right of way be carried out with special care especially at its crossing of lower Howard Creek. This is in the area where the snawning run is occurring and would be in extreme jeopardy if impacts such as those from the cleared and grubbed right of ways of Little Eastatoe Creek are allowed to occur. The proposal for construction of augmentation facilities for flow maintenance in Howard Creek do not appear justified wased on present analysis of the upper pool temperature. The staff ananlysis shown on page 3-25 makes the assumption that stratification will persist in the Whitewater arm. This would appear incorrect in light of the mixing experienced at Jocassee Dam.
If flow of proper temperature is not available, this project would do major harm to the stream community. The analysis of this potential problem must be expanded in order to consider this a potential project mitigation.
